text: @ I think the last time I really saw good VR benchmarks were form gamers nexus way back in the day. They’re really hard to do because you actually have to run them in the SteamVR runtime in order to get results that account for running distortion profiles, tracking, and reprojection overhead, but doing that makes it really difficult to make a repeatable benchmark pass since every part of it is based on the physical location of the headset, as well as which headset you’re using and if it runs native through SteamVR or through some 3rd party compositor first. Not to mention that counting FPS doesn’t really work since it will just reproject a warped version of the last frame (a lot like a cross of frame gen and Nvidia Reflex 2) on a frame drop. I really appreciate the enthusiasm of trying to find something to improve your ability to evaluate VR, but I don’t really have a great answer for you, just that running synthetic benchmarks don’t reflect actual VR performance, they basically gust give you flat screen results at a funky resolution. The title just got my hopes up that someone was doing real VR testing again. Like I said, I don’t have an easy benchmark you can run, but if I had to make a suggestion I’d say try setting up a SteamVR native headset like a Vive, Index, or big screen beyond, set render resolution to something reasonably high like 2560x2560 or 3840x3840 per eye, mount it in fixed place in the room, load a save in something heavy like fallout 4 VR or Star Wars squadrons and run some automated set of controller inputs for your benchmark pass. Then report the average frame rate as well as the reprojection and dropped frame percentage over the run. Here’s an idea too, you could use the UEVR comparability layer to reuse the benchmarks for any unreal engine 4 or 5 title you usually use for flat screen gaming. It’s a lot of work so I have no expectation that anyone, especially a smaller channel like yours would do that for a GPU review, but it would be really cool to see VR performance testing make a comeback.
